paragraphs.en: Beyond Yemen, tensions involving Iran have also raised the prospect of renewed military action by the US and Israel. Senior US officials told Axios that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu spoke with US President Donald Trump last week about the possibility of a renewed military campaign against Iran before Israel's Knesset elections are held at the end of October. The potential joint US-Israel operation could target Iran’s nuclear and military sites, sources reportedly said, adding that Netanyahu cited alleged Iranian efforts to rebuild nuclear capacity as the reason for launching new strikes. Although Trump has publicly said he has not yet decided how to proceed with Tehran, sources said both the Israel Defense Forces and US Central Command (CENTCOM) are on alert and are finalizing preparations in case he decides to order strikes. One US official told Axios that Trump told Netanyahu to "go ahead and get ready," but noted there was no firm commitment to restart military operations.
paragraphs.cn: 在也门之外，涉及伊朗的紧张局势也引发了美国和以色列可能重启军事行动的前景。美国高级官员告诉Axios，以色列总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡上周与美国总统唐纳德·特朗普讨论了在10月底以色列议会选举前重启对伊朗军事行动的可能性。据报道，消息人士称，潜在的美以联合行动可能针对伊朗的核设施和军事基地，并补充说内塔尼亚胡以伊朗据称重建核能力的努力为由要求发动新的打击。尽管特朗普公开表示尚未决定如何推进对德黑兰的行动，但消息人士称，以色列国防军和美国中央司令部均处于戒备状态，正在敲定准备工作，以防他下令发动打击。一名美国官员告诉Axios，特朗普告诉内塔尼亚胡“去准备吧”，但指出并未坚定承诺重启军事行动。

Tensions have also continued over the Strait of Hormuz, a {{12}} waterway for global energy shipments. Ali Azmaei, a senior commander in Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy, threatened to sink US warships on Tuesday if they approach the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iran's state news agency IRNA. "We are waiting for American warships to approach the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz so that we can sink them," Azmaei said in televised remarks, adding that Iranian forces are "counting down" for the encounter. US CENTCOM on Tuesday rejected Azmaei's claims, posting on X that "IRGC's navy commander has no navy. American forces and regional partners clearly control the Strait of Hormuz."
It disputed an Iranian navy commander’s remarks that Tehran controls the strategic international {{13}}, declaring that US forces had helped Gulf partners transport more than 19 million barrels of {{14}} oil through the strait on Monday.

articles.fullText:
Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthi group traded threats of retaliation on Tuesday as cross-border strikes on major cities and oil facilities continued, while Israel and the US reportedly discussed the possibility of renewing strikes against Iran before Israeli parliamentary elections.
Saudi Arabia's Civil Defense said early on Wednesday that four people were injured and 15 residential homes were damaged after debris from two intercepted cruise missiles fell in the capital Riyadh on Tuesday.
A Saudi Aramco administrative building in Dhahran, Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province, was targeted on Tuesday evening, causing a limited fire, the Saudi Press Agency reported early on Wednesday.
The Saudi-led coalition said on Tuesday night that it had intercepted multiple missiles and drones over eastern and southern Saudi Arabia. It also reported intercepting a ballistic missile targeting an administrative center in Al-Ahsa Governorate in the Eastern Province.
The coalition urged civilians to evacuate the Yemen Petroleum Company's Al-Sabaha Central Station in Houthi-held Sanaa, describing the targeted facilities as vital resources used by the Houthis to support their military operations in areas including Sanaa and Hodeidah.
Meanwhile, the Houthis said on Tuesday that Saudi warplanes and missiles carried out 104 strikes across areas held by the group over the past 24 hours.
Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Sarea claimed the attacks caused civilian casualties without giving specific figures.
Displaced Yemeni families receive food and shelter supplies provided by aid organizations in Aden, Yemen, October 12, 2026. 
The intensifying conflict is adding to the hardships faced by displaced people in Yemen, who face food shortages and health risks, according to the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA).
"Basic supplies in Taiz City are becoming increasingly scarce and expensive," said the OCHA. "Petrol prices have tripled and cooking gas is largely unavailable. Food prices have reportedly risen by about 50%, and current wheat and flour supplies could run out in less than three weeks."
The office said that the basic health of families is increasingly at risk with overcrowded displacement sites, inadequate access to clean water and minimal health services.
The OCHA added that the United Nations and its humanitarian partners have provided emergency assistance to nearly 148,000 people across Yemen since hostilities began in August.
Commercial vessels anchored in the Strait of Hormuz off Bandar Abbas, Iran, October 13, 2026. 
Beyond Yemen, tensions involving Iran have also raised the prospect of renewed military action by the US and Israel.
Senior US officials told Axios that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu spoke with US President Donald Trump last week about the possibility of a renewed military campaign against Iran before Israel's Knesset elections are held at the end of October.
The potential joint US-Israel operation could target Iran’s nuclear and military sites, sources reportedly said, adding that Netanyahu cited alleged Iranian efforts to rebuild nuclear capacity as the reason for launching new strikes.
Although Trump has publicly said he has not yet decided how to proceed with Tehran, sources said both the Israel Defense Forces and US Central Command (CENTCOM) are on alert and are finalizing preparations in case he decides to order strikes.
One US official told Axios that Trump told Netanyahu to "go ahead and get ready," but noted there was no firm commitment to restart military operations.
Tensions have also continued over the Strait of Hormuz, a strategic waterway for global energy shipments. Ali Azmaei, a senior commander in Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy, threatened to sink US warships on Tuesday if they approach the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iran's state news agency IRNA.
"We are waiting for American warships to approach the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz so that we can sink them," Azmaei said in televised remarks, adding that Iranian forces are "counting down" for the encounter.
US CENTCOM on Tuesday rejected Azmaei's claims, posting on X that "IRGC's navy commander has no navy. American forces and regional partners clearly control the Strait of Hormuz."
It disputed an Iranian navy commander’s remarks that Tehran controls the strategic international chokepoint, declaring that US forces had helped Gulf partners transport more than 19 million barrels of crude oil through the strait on Monday.

articles.title: Behind the 'distillation' pretext lies U.S. hegemony
articles.titleCn: “蒸馏”借口背后隐藏的是美国霸权
articles.summary: Viewing China’s AI through the lens of “threats”: how far will the U.S. go to distort the facts?
articles.summaryCn: 美国以“工业规模蒸馏”为由指责中国AI企业窃取技术，实为维护其技术垄断与霸权，暴露了双重标准与政治操弄。

paragraphs.en: (ECNS) -- Viewing China’s AI through the lens of “threats”: how far will the U.S. go to distort the facts? The U.S. National Security Agency (NSA), Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), and Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) jointly issued an {{0}} {{1}} Chinese AI companies of engaging in “industrial-scale” {{2}} to acquire the capabilities of advanced U.S. models.
paragraphs.cn: （中新社）——以“威胁”视角看待中国人工智能：美国究竟会歪曲事实到何种地步？美国国家安全局（NSA）、网络安全和基础设施安全局（CISA）以及联邦调查局（FBI）联合发布了一份咨询报告，指控中国人工智能公司进行“工业规模”的蒸馏，以获取美国先进模型的能力。

paragraphs.en:
The advisory also offered U.S. companies recommendations on defensive measures. On October 3, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in an interview with Axios that Chinese open-source AI models engage in “industrial distillation,” which he described as “a nice word for stealing from the U.S. models.”
China’s Ministry of Commerce had already responded to these accusations in September, stating that they were {{3}} and lacked a legal basis.
paragraphs.cn: 该咨询报告还向美国公司提供了防御措施建议。10月3日，美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特在接受Axios采访时表示，中国的开源人工智能模型进行“工业蒸馏”，他称这是“从美国模型中窃取的好听说法”。中国商务部已于9月对这些指控作出回应，称其毫无根据且缺乏法律依据。

paragraphs.en: The U.S. has repeatedly and {{4}} accused Chinese enterprises of engaging in "industrial-scale" distillation, {{5}} common practices as aggressive acts. This reflects Washington’s {{6}} and double standards. That same month, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun also weighed in on the issue, pointing out that fear-mongering, confrontation and vicious competition will only {{7}} efforts toward sound global AI governance, which serves no one’s interest. The U.S.
paragraphs.cn: 美国一再单方面指责中国企业进行“工业规模”蒸馏，将常见做法抹黑为侵略行为。这反映了华盛顿的焦虑和双重标准。同月，中国外交部发言人郭嘉昆也就此问题表态，指出制造恐慌、对抗和恶性竞争只会阻碍全球人工智能治理的健康发展，对任何人都不利。美国

paragraphs.en:
campaign to {{8}} China’s AI industry is no isolated incident. It has long been a deeply {{9}} and habitual tactic. Not long ago, the Center for a New American Security (CNAS), a Washington-based think tank, published a report exploring potential U.S. responses if China were to achieve artificial general intelligence (AGI) first, including the feasibility of military action against Chinese data centers. William Hartung, an arms analyst at the Project on Government Oversight, warned that “striking Chinese data centers based on how they might or might not be used in the future would be the height of {{10}}.”
Double standards and political {{11}} are tried-and-tested tactics in Washington.
paragraphs.cn: 抹黑中国人工智能产业的运动并非孤立事件。它长期以来一直是一种根深蒂固的习惯性策略。不久前，华盛顿智库新美国安全中心（CNAS）发布了一份报告，探讨如果中国率先实现通用人工智能（AGI），美国可能采取的应对措施，包括对中国数据中心采取军事行动的可行性。政府监督项目组织的武器分析师威廉·哈通警告说：“基于中国数据中心未来可能或不可能被如何使用而打击它们，将是最鲁莽的行为。”双重标准和政治操弄是华盛顿屡试不爽的策略。

paragraphs.en:
While the U.S. drums up the so-called “China threat,” OpenAI’s own AI agents {{12}} Hugging Face’s systems during internal cybersecurity tests, in what the company described as an “{{13}} cyber-incident.”
China’s AI development is branded as “theft,” technical exchanges within the open-source ecosystem are portrayed as a “threat,” and commercial competition is recast as a “fight for survival.” The U.S. insists on maintaining its lead while denying others the right to advance. It talks incessantly about threats posed by other countries while ignoring the risks at home. All this lays bare the true nature of Washington’s so-called “China threat” narrative: in the field of artificial intelligence, “security” is merely a pretext.

articles.fullText:
(ECNS) -- Viewing China’s AI through the lens of “threats”: how far will the U.S. go to distort the facts?
The U.S. National Security Agency (NSA), Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), and Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) jointly issued an advisory accusing Chinese AI companies of engaging in “industrial-scale” distillation to acquire the capabilities of advanced U.S. models. The advisory also offered U.S. companies recommendations on defensive measures.
On October 3, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in an interview with Axios that Chinese open-source AI models engage in “industrial distillation,” which he described as “a nice word for stealing from the U.S. models.”
China’s Ministry of Commerce had already responded to these accusations in September, stating that they were groundless and lacked a legal basis. The U.S. has repeatedly and unilaterally accused Chinese enterprises of engaging in "industrial-scale" distillation, smearing common practices as aggressive acts. This reflects Washington’s anxiety and double standards.
That same month, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun also weighed in on the issue, pointing out that fear-mongering, confrontation and vicious competition will only hamper efforts toward sound global AI governance, which serves no one’s interest.
The U.S. campaign to discredit China’s AI industry is no isolated incident. It has long been a deeply ingrained and habitual tactic.
Not long ago, the Center for a New American Security (CNAS), a Washington-based think tank, published a report exploring potential U.S. responses if China were to achieve artificial general intelligence (AGI) first, including the feasibility of military action against Chinese data centers. William Hartung, an arms analyst at the Project on Government Oversight, warned that “striking Chinese data centers based on how they might or might not be used in the future would be the height of recklessness.”
Double standards and political manipulation are tried-and-tested tactics in Washington. While the U.S. drums up the so-called “China threat,” OpenAI’s own AI agents breached Hugging Face’s systems during internal cybersecurity tests, in what the company described as an “unprecedented cyber-incident.”
China’s AI development is branded as “theft,” technical exchanges within the open-source ecosystem are portrayed as a “threat,” and commercial competition is recast as a “fight for survival.” The U.S. insists on maintaining its lead while denying others the right to advance. It talks incessantly about threats posed by other countries while ignoring the risks at home. All this lays bare the true nature of Washington’s so-called “China threat” narrative: in the field of artificial intelligence, “security” is merely a pretext. What the U.S. really seeks is an industry monopoly and technological hegemony.
When all you see is a “threat,” everything looks threatening. The development of artificial intelligence concerns the shared well-being of all humanity. What is truly unsafe is precisely the U.S. threat narrative itself, with all its contradictions.

articles.fullText:
Chinese Premier Li Qiang attended Wednesday's opening ceremony of the 140th China Import and Export Fair, also known as the Canton Fair, in Guangzhou, capital of south China's Guangdong Province, and delivered a keynote speech.
Premier Li said the fair, now in its 70th year, has offered the world a window into China's economic vitality, social progress and the deepening ties between China and the world.
An increasingly open, innovative and reliable China will bring new opportunities, fresh growth drivers and greater certainty to the world, Li said.
Li pointed out that the Canton Fair has stood the test of shifting international circumstances and kept brimming with fresh vitality, embodying plain yet profound inspirations.
"Market connectivity is not a tool for playing games, but an effective means to generate incremental growth. China is committed to promoting the continuous integration and common growth of its domestic market and the international market, and building an open world economy," the premier said.
Li said China is willing to import more high-quality products, especially high-value-added products. "We hope that more countries will work with China in the same direction, lift restrictions and actively promote the optimized and balanced development of trade," he added.
"As the largest developing country, China has always been committed to promoting common development," said the premier. "China will always be a trustworthy and reliable good friend of developing countries and is willing to join hands with the vast number of developing countries on the journey to modernization," he added.
He said China stands ready to share more market opportunities, expand more mutually beneficial cooperation and firmly safeguard the international economic and trade order with all parties.
Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, director-general of the World Trade Organization (WTO), delivered a video address noting that China has achieved remarkable development and provided rare opportunities for the world.
Highlighting the Canton Fair as a vital platform connecting China with the global economy, Okonjo-Iweala called on all parties to advance WTO reform and build an open, rules-based global trading system amid growing international uncertainties.
More than 700 representatives from nearly 90 countries and regions attended the opening ceremony.
This edition of the Canton Fair will bring together more than 30,000 exhibiting companies and about 340,000 overseas buyers.

articles.fullText:
(ECNS) -- Dennis Wilder, a U.S. international relations scholar and former CIA and National Security Council official, has sharply criticized right-wing Republican figures who attacked former Cabinet member Elaine Chao over a visit to a Shanghai kindergarten.
Some right-wing figures have criticized Chao and her husband, Republican Senator Mitch McConnell, over her June visit to a kindergarten in Shanghai, accusing her of having close ties to China.
Chao served as U.S. Secretary of Labor in the administration of George W. Bush from 2001 to 2009 and as U.S. Secretary of Transportation in the first administration of Donald Trump from 2017 to 2021.
On June 14, she attended an event at a kindergarten in Malu township, Jiading district, Shanghai, showcasing the school's achievements and celebrating the graduation of its senior kindergarten class of 2026.
According to information previously released by local authorities, the kindergarten was renovated in 1994 with a $100,000 donation from Chao's father, James S.C. Chao. The school was later renamed after his father, Zhao Yiren.
The visit has since become a target of political attacks against Chao and her husband McConnell.
Tensions between McConnell and the Republican Party's right-wing populist wing have grown in recent years. Some figures in the faction have sought to blame Chao for McConnell's clashes with them, making unsubstantiated allegations that she has ties to Beijing and acts on China's instructions to influence her husband.
The Daily Caller, a conservative media outlet aligned with the party's right wing, went further in a recent article targeting Chao.
It claimed the kindergarten had military connections and suggested it served as a meeting place for Chao and Chinese officials. The article pointed to children's performances featuring themes related to the spirit of the Long March and dances in camouflage clothing as evidence.
In a post on X on Tuesday, Wilder said he was "petrified," mocking the outlet's portrayal of the children's activities as a security concern.
"Combat training for children in diapers. Please stop. You are embarrassing yourself," he said.
In a separate post, Wilder ridiculed the outlet's claims, writing: "Good God! Supporting a kindergarten in Shanghai is now considered treasonous? Those 3-year-olds look extremely dangerous to me! The Daily Caller is really reaching on this one."

（中新社）——美国国际关系学者、前中央情报局和国家安全委员会官员丹尼斯·怀尔德严厉批评了右翼共和党人士，他们因前内阁成员赵小兰访问上海一所幼儿园而对她进行攻击。一些右翼人士批评赵小兰及其丈夫、共和党参议员米奇·麦康奈尔，指责她与中国关系密切，起因是她6月访问了上海的一所幼儿园。赵小兰曾在乔治·W·布什政府中担任美国劳工部长。

布什政府时期，2001年至2009年担任美国劳工部长，并在唐纳德·特朗普第一任期内，2017年至2021年担任美国交通部长。6月14日，她出席了上海嘉定区马陆镇一所幼儿园的活动，展示该校成就并庆祝2026届大班学生毕业。根据当地政府此前发布的信息，该幼儿园于1994年由赵小兰的父亲赵锡成捐赠10万美元进行翻新。

该校后来以她的父亲赵以仁命名。此次访问随后成为针对赵小兰及其丈夫麦康奈尔的政治攻击目标。近年来，麦康奈尔与共和党右翼民粹主义派系之间的紧张关系不断加剧。该派系的一些人士试图将麦康奈尔与他们的冲突归咎于赵小兰，提出毫无根据的指控，称她与北京有联系，并按照中国的指示影响她的丈夫。与共和党右翼结盟的保守派媒体《每日来电》在最近一篇针对赵小兰的文章中更进一步。

该文章声称这所幼儿园与军方有联系，并暗示它是赵小兰与中国官员会面的场所。文章以儿童表演长征精神相关主题的节目和穿着迷彩服跳舞作为证据。周二，怀尔德在X平台上发帖称他“吓坏了”，嘲讽该媒体将儿童活动描绘成安全关切。“穿着尿布的儿童进行战斗训练。请停止。

你这是在让自己难堪，”他说。在另一条帖子中，怀尔德嘲笑该媒体的说法，写道：“天哪！支持上海的一所幼儿园现在被视为叛国？那些3岁的孩子在我看来极其危险！《每日来电》这次真是牵强附会。”
